doc.title: Jon Hendricks — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Social Call for Ernestine Anderson; writing a song a week
summary: He wrote Social Call, recalls writing a song a week in Toledo, and Johnny Mercer's astonishment.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: What were some – did you write other songs that were outside of the jazz idiom during that period, and for other people?

Yeah. I wrote Social Call, which it really wasn’t outside the jazz idiom, but it was a kind of a swing ballad. At that time Ernestine Anderson was married to Art Farmer. And Art Farmer – she was having a child at that time. She was pregnant when she recorded Social Call with she and Art’s first baby. Art and Gigi Gryce had the quintet – I think it was the Jazz Lab Quintet – together. Later it was Donald Byrd, but the first one was Art Farmer. I wrote Social Call, and she recorded it.
What was the first song that you wrote lyrics for? Do you remember that?
I wrote a song a week for the group I was with in Toledo, words and music. When I told Johnny Mercer that I wrote a song a week, he said, “Man, you’re crazy.”
Do you still work that hard?
Do you still work hard like that?
Oh sure. But he couldn’t believe that.
He said, “Man, we take months to write a song.” He says, “How could you write a song a week?” I said, “That’s what they wanted.” I thought, if they wanted it, that’s what everybody did.
